Locked in: Saturday 13 December 2025, 3–7pm in Darwin.

Here’s a concise plan for park, food, and activities based on your needs.

1) Park suggestions (central, shade, toilets, accessible, kid‑friendly)
These are good candidates to investigate/book with Council if needed:

1. Bicentennial Park / The Esplanade (central Darwin)
- Why it fits: Very central, lots of open grass and shade, ocean views, paths suitable for wheelchairs and older locals.
- Facilities: Shelters, seating, paths, toilets nearby (check exact section of the park; some parts are closer to toilets than others).
- Kid suitability: Plenty of space to run around, but not a “contained” playground—good for ball games and picnic games.
- Watch-outs: Some sections can be quite exposed; pick a spot with established trees or a shelter.

2. East Point Reserve
- Why it fits: Popular for community gatherings, big open spaces, generally good shade, walking paths.
- Facilities: BBQs and shelters in several spots, toilets in the reserve (check which area you’d use), decent parking.
- Kid suitability: Heaps of room for running games, frisbee, etc.
- Watch-outs: Slightly less “CBD central” than The Esplanade, but still well known and accessible.

3. Jingili Water Gardens (if you’re okay being a bit off‑CBD)
- Why it fits: Shady, relaxed atmosphere with paths, lawns, water features.
- Facilities: Toilets, paths for wheelchairs, some picnic/BBQ areas (confirm current status with Council).
- Kid suitability: Very good—kids can explore, but you’ll still want some supervision around water features.

If you want the most central and “community picnic” vibe, I’d suggest:
- First preference: A shaded area at Bicentennial Park/The Esplanade close to toilets and parking.
- Backup: East Point Reserve BBQ/shelter area.

Next step for you:  
- Check with City of Darwin website / parks info which specific area has:
  - BBQs + shelters that can be reserved
  - Toilets within a short, flat walk
  - Good parking and accessible paths

2) Food plan – BBQ + bring‑a‑plate (for 40–60 people)
Keep it simple and predictable:

Core BBQ items (organiser-provided):
- Sausages + veggie sausages
- Sliced bread / rolls
- Onions, basic salad (coleslaw / garden salad)
- Condiments: tomato sauce, BBQ sauce, mustard, mayo
- Vegetarian option: veggie patties or grilled veg/haloumi
- Cold drinks: water, cordial / soft drinks (esky with ice)

Bring‑a‑plate guidance (for invite):
- Ask people to bring:
  - A salad OR a dessert (e.g., fruit platter, slice, cake)
  - Clearly label anything that’s vegetarian / gluten‑free / contains nuts
- Make it clear: “Please don’t bring foods that need reheating or complex prep on site.”

Equipment checklist:
- BBQ tools: tongs, spatulas, oil spray, foil
- Serving: disposable or reusable plates, cups, cutlery, napkins, serving spoons
- Cold storage: eskies + ice
- Hygiene: hand sanitiser, wipes, rubbish bags, paper towel
- Comfort: a few spare picnic rugs, folding chairs for older locals, maybe a marquee or two for extra shade

Given your moderate budget, you can:
- Cover all BBQ meats, bread, basics + drinks from your budget.
- Rely on guests for salads/desserts via bring‑a‑plate.

3) Simple activity plan (3–7pm, families + older locals)

Suggested run‑sheet:
- 3:00–3:30pm – Arrival and settling in
  - Light background music.
  - Welcome table/sign-in (if you need contact details).
  - Cold drinks and snacks available.

- 3:30–5:00pm – Food + casual games
  - Start BBQ around 3:30.
  - Low‑energy, inclusive options for older locals:
    - Shaded seating area with conversation tables.
    - Simple card or board games on tables (dominoes, cards, etc.).
  - For kids and families:
    - Ball games (soccer, cricket, frisbee).
    - Simple organised games: tug‑of‑war, egg‑and‑spoon race, three‑legged race.
    - If budget allows: hire or borrow a couple of lawn games (giant Jenga, quoits, bocce).

- 5:00–5:30pm – Short “community moment”
  - Quick welcome / thanks over a portable speaker.
  - Acknowledgement of Country if appropriate for your group.
  - Any short announcements or recognition (e.g., volunteers, long‑time locals).

- 5:30–6:30pm – Relaxed social time
  - More casual games, dessert/tea/coffee if you provide it.
  - Consider a small kids’ activity table (colouring, craft) next to the main group so older locals can watch and chat.

- 6:30–7:00pm – Wind‑down and pack‑up
  - Start packing up food safely, manage rubbish.
  - Final walks through the area to leave it tidy.

4) Quick decisions I need from you to refine this:
- Which park would you like to target first (Bicentennial Park/The Esplanade vs East Point vs Jingili Water Gardens)?
- Do you want to keep activities very simple (balls + a couple of classic games), or add one “feature” (e.g., hire a face‑painter, lawn games set, or acoustic musician)?

If you tell me the park you prefer and how “big” you want the activities, I can:
- Draft a short description/“blurb” you can use for flyers, Facebook, or emails.
- Give you a compact checklist you can hand to volunteers. </action>

  - BBQ setup, cooking, food safety, manage helpers.

- Volunteer C – Games & General Support  
  - Set up balls/lawn games, run a few simple kids’ games, help where needed.  
- (Optional) Volunteer D – Pack‑up & Rubbish Lead  
  - Coordinates pack‑up and final site check.

  - Quick briefing for volunteers: roles, timings, safety.

  - Check BBQs are clean and working.
  - Set up BBQ tools, food prep area, hand sanitiser.
- Welcome (B):
  - Set up welcome/info table (signage, basic info, hand sanitiser).
- Games (C):
  - Put out balls, lawn games, a couple of simple table games.
- Pack‑up (D):
  - Set up rubbish bags/points and spare bin liners.

3:00–3:30pm – ARRIVALS & DRINKS
- Welcome (B):
  - Greet people, direct plates to food table, point to toilets and seating.
- Richard:
  - Circulate, welcome older locals, check anyone with access needs is comfortable.
- Games (C):
  - Light casual games for kids (balls, frisbee), keep it low‑key at start.

3:30–5:00pm – BBQ & MAIN PICNIC
- BBQ Lead (A):
  - Start and run BBQ. Keep vegetarian items separate.
  - Monitor food safety (no food left in sun too long, covered where possible).
- Welcome (B):
  - Keep food tables tidy, ensure salads/desserts are labelled where possible.
- Games (C):
  - Run simple games: e.g., relay/three‑legged race, tug‑of‑war, gentle ball games.
  - Keep an eye out for safety and include shy kids.
- Richard:
  - Move between BBQ, welcome, and games, fill gaps, chat with attendees.

5:00–5:30pm – COMMUNITY MOMENT & DESSERT
- Richard:
  - Short welcome/thank‑you over portable speaker:
    - Welcome everyone, Acknowledgement of Country (if appropriate).
    - Thank volunteers/attendees, mention Darwin Community Connect.
    - Invite people to stay, play games, and connect.
- All:
  - Shift focus to desserts/tea/coffee if provided.
  - Encourage mixing between families and older locals.

5:30–6:15pm – RELAX & SOCIAL TIME
- Games (C):
  - Keep lawn games going, but relaxed.
- Welcome (B):
  - Check in with older locals, see if anyone needs help (chairs, shade).
- Richard:
  - Circulate and gather quick informal feedback.

6:15–7:00pm – PACK‑UP & FINAL CHECK
- Pack‑up Lead (D):
  - Coordinate pack‑up: tables, chairs, games, leftover food, eskies.
  - Organise rubbish collection; check area is cleaner than you found it.
- BBQ Lead (A):
  - Turn off and clean BBQs, safely store or dispose of leftover food.
- Games (C):
  - Collect balls/lawn games, check nothing left behind.
- Richard:
  - Final walk‑through, thank remaining attendees and volunteers.
  - Confirm all equipment is accounted for.

WET‑WEATHER PLAN (SUMMARY)
- By ~12:00pm:
  - Richard checks weather and park conditions.
  - If unsafe or very wet:
    - Decide: postpone OR move to East Point Reserve.
    - Post message via your usual channels + send SMS/email:
      - Use the prepared wet‑weather/postponement wording.
  - Ensure volunteers are notified by group message or call.

KEY REMINDERS
- Safety: Watch BBQ, kids near roads/paths, slips in wet grass.  
- Accessibility: Keep clear paths, reserve shaded seating for older locals and anyone with mobility issues.  
- Visibility: Signs/banners where people can see you from the path/parking.
